title: WPSB/162/2010 of SHIV KUMAR SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 162 of 2010
Shiv Kumar Singh. ........... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. ............ Respondents
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand / respondent Nos. 1 to 3.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.

BARIN GHOSH, C. J. (Oral)
 In the instant case, the original charge-sheet was issued on 31st
December, 1999 by the Inquiry Officer, which is not permissible. But, we
have not gone into that question having regard to the fact that, since 31st
December, 1999 until filing of the writ petition in 2010, no challenge was
thrown to the same. The supplementary charge-sheet was issued on 11th
May, 2000. While the original charge-sheet was replied on 28th January,
2000, the supplementary charge-sheet was replied on 23rd June, 2000. A
look at these charge-sheets will indicate that the basic allegation against
the petitioner was that the files relating to the court work were not
maintained properly, as the register of register (Missal Band Register) was
not up to date, and the files were not consigned to record room as per
rules and non recording of gist of the order in the Missal Band Register.
The other charge was of serious nature. In that, it was contended that the
land, belonging to the State, was mutated in favour of third parties in the
revenue record without any approval of the competent authority.
2. These charges were enquired into. Before the Inquiry Officer, not a
single witness appeared to prove the charges. Petitioner went before the
Inquiry Officer, repeated denial as was given by him in his replies to the
charge-sheets and produced mutation orders passed by his superiors in the

2
Revenue Department. Surprisingly, the Inquiry Officer held that, on the
basis of records, as were produced, he is satisfied that the charges stand
proved. While doing so, he commented that the orders of mutation passed
by the officers of the Revenue Department have not been independently
proved by the petitioner. On the basis of the report of the inquiry,
petitioner was given a show-cause, why he should not be dismissed from
service and, later, by a punishment order, petitioner was demoted to the
post of Chainman from the post of Survey Lekhpal. The order of the
disciplinary authority having been confirmed by the appellate authority,
petitioner approached the Tribunal and failed before it. Surprisingly, the
Tribunal, while dealing with the matter, did not take note of the fact that
the petitioner had produced the approval report / orders pertaining to
mutation before the Inquiry Officer and how the Inquiry Officer dealt
with those reports / orders. The Tribunal miserably failed to discharge its
duties pertaining to the Application that was dealt with by it in the matter
of evidence that was to be brought on record for proving the charges. It
was well within the competence of the Tribunal to declare the inquiry
report absolutely void, as the same was without any evidence, inasmuch
as, no evidence of whatsoever nature was produced before the Inquiry
Officer by the State Government to prove the charges. As the Inquiry
Officer had put the ball on the petitioner, so the Tribunal did by holding
out that it was obligatory on the part of the petitioner to discharge him
from the allegations as were made in the charge-sheets. We are really
surprised.
3. For the reasons indicated above, we allow the writ petition; quash
the order of the Tribunal as well as the order of the appellate authority and
of the disciplinary authority. Consequentially, petitioner should be
deemed to be a Survey Lekhpal all throughout.

(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C. J.)
 05.03.2014 05.03.2014
G
